headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.4260). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 11 studies yielded an effect size of 0.97 (95% CI: 0.92–1.01), indicating no statistically significant association between caffeine and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by moderate heterogeneity (I² = 45.93%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.
